channel.title: Comments for page "Exploration Log 1689-I"
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Exploration Log 1689-I"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Rediscovered this one, rereading — this is a Good exploration log. It keeps a steady pace because each log tells you only exactly what you need to know. They're in a potato dimension, and they're digging potatoes. Despite how, honestly, bare the premise is, the log has a lot going for it. It's rich in personality. There's a slew of great one-liners, too.

I'm thinking that on the modern Wiki, we have a dearth of these kinds of exploration logs with novel concepts, that are easy to jump into and contain more than the sum of their parts. Not to knock what we have now, though, or claim what we had then was superior; this is just a nice palate cleanser!

item.content:encoded:
1)Am I the only one who doesn't understand why none of the potatoes show signs of attempting to grow into potato plants?

2)Spudzerland could probably be saved by the introduction of something like potato blight, since it's obvious that nothing of the sort exists in this world given the fact that it isn't freaking everywhere. Sure it'll probably take a few centuries, but hey, it's worth a shot. Hell, stick the bag in that one time-dilating microwave and the two species might become the basis for an entire ecosystem, aided no doubt by all the microbes introduced to Spudzerland by the ninety days worth of excrement doubtlessly left behind by Task Force Tater.

item.content:encoded:
You know, I think about all the horrific things this site has to offer: the Scarlet King, the endless cavalcade of monsters and phenomena that kill you in horrifically specific ways, the fairy world that mutilates you if you name it, the cabal of hideously inbred cannibal mole people under Vienna (read that one yesterday, Jesus F-ing Christ), etc. Sometimes I like to come back to articles like this to un-clench/unwind, and it always makes me happy when I stumble on a new one. I like when writers remember that the Foundation deals in ALL things bizarre and weird, not just the creepy/world-ending stuff.

+1 Just because something seems silly or stupid, that doesn't mean it's not important.
